rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Inductive effect: permanent polarisation through σ bonds, dies out by C3–C4 (−I: NO2, X, COOH; +I: alkyl) — 'through sigma, distance-limited' is the definition mark.  ·  Trick 2: Resonance: delocalisation through π bonds/ lone pairs; stability order: resonance structures with full octets and least charge separation dominate.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Trick 3: Hyperconjugation: 'no-bond resonance' — α-C–H σ electrons delocalise into an adjacent p-orbital; more α-H → more stable alkene/carbocation (Saytzeff and Markovnikov both rest on this).  ·  Trick 4: Carbocation stability: benzylic/allylic (resonance) > 3° (hyperconjugation + I) > 2° > 1° > methyl — the ordering question is a favourite.  ·  define + example each sub-idea: inductive effect, resonance, hyperconjugation.
